text.p: Demand for shares being sold by Moroccan credit firm Maghrebail saw the offer oversubscribed 18 times, in part thanks to foreign interest, the firm's chairman Mohamed Amin Benjelloun said on Thursday.
"Sale of 20 percent of Maghrebail capital has been oversubscribed 18 times," he told a news conference in Morocco's financial capital.
The number of subscribers reached 25,840 of whom 44 were foreign institutions mainly Anglo-Saxon, he said.
"Foreigners' enthusiasm for the shares was very important," Benjelloun added.
Shares were offered in two categories. One tranche of 102,532 shares was devoted to the public, with a similar tranche offered to institutions.
The firm's new issue worth 82 million dirhams ($8.63 million) brought its capital to 102.5 million dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur hold respectively 27.5 percent and 11.8 percent of Maghrebail.
Benjelloun said earlier the firm had a 23.6 percent share of Morocco's leasing market in 1996.
